checks: Since C is compact, only finitely many integer bases are sampled. Each nonempty compact convex fiber has Hausdorff dimension equal to its affine dimension, so q is their maximum. Fibers of dimension smaller than q are null for the reference measure. Absolute continuity then forces every positive input fiber on either side to have dimension q.

The cross input bases are in the same original parity class and so p=(z+w)/2 is integer. Convexity gives the inclusion of the fiber Minkowski midpoint set into the actual nonempty C_p. The direction of that sum is the sum of the two directions, since holding either endpoint fixed realizes the differences from the other. Both directions have dimension q and the target dimension is at most q. They must coincide and the target also has dimension q.

Positive total mass on both sides supplies one comparison fiber on each side. Comparing any opposite-side pair then gives the same direction for every participating fiber, with no claim across unrelated parity classes.

For two affine hulls b_z+L and b_w+L with b_z,b_w perpendicular to L, the averaged affine hull is (b_z+b_w)/2+L. Its inclusion in the q-dimensional target gives equality of affine hulls. Two different pairs with the same p therefore yield the same unique orthogonal offset.
